title: I Walked Out of the Warehouse Family Meeting Mid-Sentence

parts.text: I stood up in the family meeting when they called skipped lunch loyalty. I am thirty-one, night warehouse, Casio still on my wrist. Vince said we were a family for the fourth time. Families do not badge you into hour eleven. The break room coffee was burnt, classic. I put my badge on the table. I did not make a speech. I said I am going to lunch, actually, and then I went. Marisol came too, then two more. We ate gas-station taquitos on the tailgate. They tasted like rubber and freedom, which is a strong seasoning. HR called it a walkout. It was a lunch. They posted real break times the next week. I did not get promoted. I got a taquito stain on my vest that would not wash out. I consider it a pin. Family is a word I save for people who do not time my chewing. Vince said, "Sit down, we're a family" I said, "Families eat lunch" Vince asked if I was done. I said after protein. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink.

social.video_title: I left the family meeting to eat an actual lunch
social.description: Burnt coffee, taquitos, a badge on the table. HR called it a walkout. Would you have stood up on the fourth family?
